commentPreTextItems: [{'type': 'HTML', 'html': ' 7.28pm More red than blue in the Ahmedabad stands, but that is not surprising, is it? The red carpet is laid out as defending champions RCB walk out. GT follow them, with Gill leading the way. We will have the national anthem first. Aight, here come the two GT openers, Shubman Gill and B Sai Sudharsan. How much will Sai Suds be thinking about the two hit-wickets? Just an FYI: We have two hours of back-up time tonight and need a minimum of 10-overs-a-side game. Jacob Duffy has the new ball, and not Bhuvneshwar Kumar. That's interesting. He is over the wicket with a slip in place to Sai Sudharsan. LET'S GO! Kaushal: "This IPL has witnessed batting records be shattered but has been a little short of nail-biting thrillers compared to the last few seasons. Hope we have a last ball finish here!!" On that note, with five minutes to go to the start, here's Ashish Alien: "Thank god, the final is not at Chinnaswamy. Its raining cats and dogs here, would've wasted a lot of time. But still I heard lots of cheers from my damp neighbourhood when RCB won the toss. " Alfred: "@Atul same for purple cap" Atul: "Today if Gill or Sai fall before overtaking Vaibhav in the orange cap race, then RCB will win. Basically, orange cap and cup for the titans or neither " Yep, Ashish and I were discussing just that earlier. I think GT will be happy as of now because their stronger suit will be on show in the second half. VinayMudunuru: "Buttler will have one of the biggest nights of his career!!" Sam: "No Phil Salt but might be better that way…" Yeah, guess he hasn't fully recovered. RCB have played without him for a while now, so it shouldn't be too big an issue Jashan: "So it's Romario over Suyash..." Vikram: "Conventional wisdom would have said Bat first. But if RCB restrict GT under 200, then Kohli will gobble this chase and stay till the end. GT needs to be aggressive, this is the same pitch where India scored 250 in the finals. This match will be tasty affair." Prasidh should be GT's sub going by what was said at the toss GT sub options Prasidh Krishna, Glenn Phillips, Anuj Rawat, Kumar Kushagra, Sai Kishore Gujarat Titans: 1 Shubman Gill (capt), 2 B Sai Sudharsan, 3 Jos Buttler (wk), 4 Jason Holder, 5 Washington Sundar, 6 Rahul Tewatia, 7 Rashid Khan, 8 Nishant Sindhu, 9 Kagiso Rabada, 10 Arshad Khan, 11 Mohammed Siraj Venky Iyer will likely come in as the sub for RCB RCB sub options - Venkatesh Iyer, Kanishk Chohan, Swapnil Singh, Abhinandan Singh, Jordan Cox Royal Challengers Bengaluru: 1 Virat Kohli, 2 Devdutt Padikkal, 3 Rajat Patidar (capt), 4 Krunal Pandya, 5 Tim David, 6 Jitesh Sharma (wk), 7 Romario Shepherd, 8 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 9 Josh Hazlewood, 10 Jacob Duffy, 11 Rasikh Salam Shubman Gill, GT captain We'd have batted. Hope to put runs and them under pressure. Typical wicket, third match on it. Might be movement for 2-3 overs for pacers. We're feeling fresh and ready. One of the biggest stadiums, always a privilege to play here. Arshad comes back in place of Sai (Kishore) Rajat Patidar, RCB captain Good wicket, won't change in the 40 overs. Will try to get them out early. Lot of memories from last year, but it's 2026 now. Have to do our best to win. Important to stay in the present. Love to play here because of the crowd. Same team 7pm Ravi Shastri out for the toss. Javagal Srinath hands over the coin to Patidar, who'll spin the coin. Heads is the call, it's tails. RCB bowl Huge cheers Pitch Pitch No. 6, equidistant, both square boundaries 66 metres. Aaron Finch says it's a mix-soil pitch, good for batting. It's very even and flat. Doesn't mean it's a belter. Might be slightly slow, might not spin with the soil composition. Ian Bishop says there'll be a high percentage of balls on a good length from pacers, and then the preference of hit-the-deck bowlers to go good or short of good length. Win the toss and chase, says Finch, will get better and better. Karthik Siram : "Any signs of a new debutant today? I feel Gurnoor Brar could be a great surprise pick for the final. An element of surprise can be a powerful weapon." Highly doubt it Krishna Sumanth: "who is going to be the 'Ben Cutting' of Gujarat tonight?" Eric: "Whether Kohli makes it through the powerplay or not is going to be key. When he does everybody gets their ideal entry point and when he gets out early we've seen RCB get into trouble especially with Jitesh and Shepherd out of form" Nikhil Parupall: "Good Evening from Singapore!! 9:30PM and i am ready to celebrate with 2time winner .." 6:50pm Under 10 minutes to go for the toss. Attendance is healthy, the roads outside the ground have been packed for a while. Gill is suited up for the toss, he run down the stairs. Sunshine's still there but floodlights are also taking effect. Nehra has a small chat with GIll. Captain inspects the good length of the pitch. Celine : "Greetings from Helsinki! Being a RCB fan, I'm nervous cos the game is with home advantage to GT. Go RCB, ee sala cup namdeh!" Arul: "GT didn't have much prep time, I think Rcb today.." Virat: "GT team has mainly 5 players (2 batters, 2 bowlers and 1 all rounder) and if RCB will have strategies to handle these 5 players then they will easily win the match. " With Rashid, Prasidh and Holder, they don't really have a weak link in their bowling, do they? Also, Buttler's still great with bat With 45 minutes to go, coach Andy Flower is on one knee, in the middle of RCB's huddle, giving a pep talk. Players and staff forming two concentric circles around him, it's a long talk. Kohli follows with choppy, pointy gestures into the palm while speaking. A bit of applause and the huddle breaks Hus Silverado : "All 3 matches in the playoffs have been won by the team losing the toss..So don't be surprised if it happens today as well !!!" Now this for me is more of a hot take Gummalla: "Unpopular opinion: GT are being underestimated. RCB may be favorites on paper, but finals are won by handling pressure, not hype. GT for me." GT at home are favourites, no? 6:40pm Thanks, Ashish. Hey all. I'm afraid toss-winner might be the match-winner tonight. If the team losing the toss wins, it'll be quite the achievement. The point is there's no running away from the destroyer of free will that is T20 dynamics. There's also the other cliche - bowling wins teams tournaments. While GT has arguably the strongest attack in the comp, RCB have a couple of the best new-ball bowlers but can their middle-overs bowling stand up too? shishank dahiya: "Any rain around ?" Not at the ground, no From Shashank, our rep at the ground: RCB leaning towards a similar combination from Q1. Duffy & Hazlewood marking run-ups. I am off for a coffee. Meanwhile, please welcome RCB fan Ekanth into the comms seat for the first time today. Who's winning this, Ekanth? 6.30pm Here is a potentially controversial statement. Virat Kohli's IPL of 2026 has been as good as if not better than his IPL of 2016. Scoring 973 runs at a strike rate of 152.03 is an extraordinary feat, but his 600 runs at 164.38 this year are more indicative of a proper team plan from RCB and Kohli slotting in in that plan perfectly. Here's a banger of an article from Sidharth Monga on why Kohli's 2026 could be better than Kohli's 2016. Dhruv: "Jason Holder has changed the fortunes of GT in second half, I expect him to play the decisive role tonight." Shadow-Shell: "5 seasons, 4 playoffs qualification, 3rd final, playing for theird 2nd trophy. Is GT the new CSK? Especially with the recent decline of CSK" 6.20pm When Rajat Patidar leads RCB out for their second straight IPL final in Ahmedabad on Sunday, he will have the chance to join an elite list of captains who have won back-to-back IPL titles. But his route towards this peak has been remarkably different. When MS Dhoni completed the double for Chennai Super Kings in 2010-11, he had already established himself as a bona fide great. By the time Rohit Sharma led Mumbai Indians to consecutive titles in 2019-20, he was already a multiple-time IPL-winning captain. Patidar, in comparison, last played for India in early 2024, and was dropped after poor returns in three Tests. He hasn't come close to national selection since. Yet, the sheer weight of his runs at IPL 2026 - 486 runs at a strike rate of 196.76 - has brought him back into conversations for a T20I spot. Here's Shashank Kishore on the quiet captain. Shaurya: "It's so crazy to me that Bhuvi denied RCB the trophy 10 years ago when i was a little kid...now i my early 20s again but this time he has joined forces with VK and just hoping they don't break my heart again..!!" 6.10pm The RCB and GT buses are making their way to the ground. The stands are filling in nice and early. GT face the unenviable task of playing a third game, at a third venue, in six days on Sunday. Their captain Shubman Gill isn't too perturbed by it, though he conceded that their well-rested opponents may have an edge heading into the final. Usually, IPL knockouts are held in only two venues, but this year's scheduling has given the winner of Qualifier 1 a bigger advantage. 6pm Rajat Patidar isn't thinking of the final as possibly being legacy-defining. Neither is he stressed about T20I selection or India captaincy. He simply wants to enjoy the occasion RCB have worked doubly hard for. "I've never thought about what other captains have done before or whether I want to compete with someone," he said. "As an individual, my journey has had its ups and downs, but I've never focused on that [captaincy, legacy]." 5.50pm A decade ago, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and SRH denied Virat Kohli's RCB the title. Ten years later, Virat Kohli is at the centre of RCB's hopes again. He is already an IPL champion once and will have Bhuvneshwar with him as they align to achieve the common goal - the IPL trophy. Here's Shashank Kishore on the contrasting journeys of Kohli and Bhuvneshwar but how they are getting together to help RCB achieve a second IPL title. Vas: "Will Salt be fit to play? Romario or Duffy? Lots to ponder for RCB." 5.40pm For the last eight straight IPLs, the team winning Qualifier 1 has gone on to become champion. Does that come true again? RCB had beaten GT quite comfortably in Qualifier 1. But, they lost to GT in Ahmedabad in the league stage, bowled out for 155. They've won only three of their seven away or neutral games in IPL 2026. But, all of that can be tossed to the wayside if any of their match-winners come off. GT's campaign has been built on the hard work of Kagiso Rabada and Mohammed Siraj; in particular the unstinting way they attack oppositions in the powerplay. Both quicks have been encouraged to go pace-on. Both quicks have been remarkable at assessing the vulnerabilities of specific batters. Both quicks have the potential to break the game early. Here's Alagappan Muthu's preview for the final. 5.30pm IPL S19. The Final. After 64 days, 70 league matches, and three playoffs, we have two teams fighting for the crowning glory. Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Gujarat Titans. RCB, adored by millions, envied by millions. One of IPL's nearly there teams finally broke the duck in the 18th season. They are back in the 19th, bigger and better and hungrier than ever before. Then there's GT, one of the IPL's newest teams. Unlike their opponents, they wasted no time in getting their hands on the silverware. They won it in their debut season in 2022 and then nearly defended it in 2023. The captaincy has changed hands since then, but with a well-rounded team who are at home, they are worthy title contenders. So, where does the IPL trophy go? Does it remain in Ahmedabad or does it travel to Bengaluru for the second straight season? I am Ashish Pant, nice and early because why not. There's lots to build up, lots to look forward and lots to dissect. Sit back and relax, one of these two teams is going to double their IPL championship count. '}]
